t: Texas declared independence from Mexico on 2 March 1836, after Santa Anna's Siete Leyes centralised the Mexican republic and he began enforcing laws against slavery, which Mexico had abolished in 1829 and which the Texians refused to end.

Its 1836 constitution made slavery a cornerstone of the state: slaves could not be freed without the consent of Congress, Congress could pass no law against slavery or the slave trade, and no free person of African descent could reside permanently in the republic.
Only seven nations recognised Texas, and its claim to the Rio Grande as its border, disputed by Mexico throughout, passed to the United States at annexation and led to the Mexican–American War.
dyk: In 1839 Texas became the first nation in the world to enact a homestead exemption, under which creditors cannot seize a person's primary residence.
ev: On 2 October hostilities between Texian settlers and Mexican troops open at the Battle of Gonzales, the first engagement of the Texas Revolution.
On 2 March the Convention of 1836 proclaims the Texas Declaration of Independence; David G. Burnet becomes interim president.
On 21 April major fighting ends, and the Treaties of Velasco, signed by Santa Anna as a prisoner, secure Texas's independence, which the Mexican Congress refuses to recognise.
On 3 March President Andrew Jackson appoints Alcée La Branche chargé d'affaires, the United States officially recognising the republic.
President Mirabeau B. Lamar moves the capital to the new town of Austin; the Lone Star Flag is adopted and France recognises Texas on 25 September.
After 34 Comanche leaders are massacred at peace talks in San Antonio, Buffalo Hump leads the Great Raid of 1840 to the Gulf coast; the Comanches are caught at the Battle of Plum Creek.
On 11 September Adrián Woll's 1,400 Mexican troops capture San Antonio; Texans fight at the Battle of Salado Creek while 53 surrendered volunteers are massacred nearby.
On 29 December Texas is annexed and admitted as the 28th state of the United States; power passes from the republic on 19 February 1846.

f.capital: Washington-on-the-Brazos, Harrisburg, Galveston, Velasco and Columbia (1836), Houston (1837), Austin (1839)
f.founder: The delegates of the Convention of 1836; David G. Burnet interim president, Sam Houston the first elected president
f.predecessor: Mexican Texas, part of the state of Coahuila y Tejas in the Mexican republic
f.successor: The State of Texas, the 28th state of the United States (annexed 29 December 1845)
